criterion: On the public event page the ground, the headings and the hairlines all derive from one stored key colour.
evaluation_rule: A KEY COLOUR is the single colour stored on an event and used to derive that page's whole palette. Answer yes when the ground, the heading colour and the hairline colour on a seeded event page read as tints of one hue, and two seeded event pages read as two different hues. Answer no when the page uses the plain paper ground with the default ink.

criterion: On the landing route the brand mark carries the pink accent the palette reserves for the mark, the invite badge and one link hue.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the brand mark in the bar is drawn in a hot pink and that same pink appears only on the invite badge and one inline link elsewhere. Answer no when the mark is drawn in the body ink, or when the pink is used as a general decorative fill.

criterion: Body text across the signed-in screens sits in the single near-black ink the palette pins.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when running text on the signed-in screens is one near-black throughout, with lighter greys reserved for secondary and tertiary text. Answer no when body text appears in two or more unrelated dark colours.

criterion: On the public event page each cover tile carries a glow layer, a sheen layer and a blurred copy beneath the image.
evaluation_rule: A GLOW is a soft coloured halo spilling onto the ground around the tile, and a SHEEN is a highlight inside the tile. Answer yes when the tile shows a coloured halo around its edges and a lit highlight across its face. Answer no when the tile sits flat on the ground with a hard edge.

criterion: An event page whose derived ground would leave its own ink unreadable falls back to the plain paper ground and tells the host the cover is pale.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when an event whose cover produces a very light ground renders on the plain paper ground with the default ink and shows the host a message about the cover. Answer no when the page renders text that is too faint to read against its own ground.

criterion: The discover list states the empty-result heading the copy deck pins when a filter matches nothing.
evaluation_rule: Compare the visible heading against the string No Events Found, ignoring surrounding whitespace, letter case and a trailing full stop. Answer yes when that heading appears with a sentence beneath and one action beside it. Answer no when the list renders as a blank area.

criterion: The themed ground of a public event page fades in once and then holds still.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the coloured ground appears with a single slow fade on first load and stays static afterwards. Answer no when the ground pulses, loops or re-fades on scroll.

criterion: Cover tiles carry a corner curve that tracks the tile aspect ratio rather than a constant radius.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the corner curve on a wide tile differs from the curve on a square tile of the same design. Answer no when every tile shows the same corner curve at every shape.

criterion: On the guest list one hue marks a failed action, a second marks a completed action and a third marks a pending action.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the three meanings each own one hue and those three hues appear only on state markers. Answer no when one of the three hues is also used as a decorative fill or a background.

criterion: Every element that moves shares one motion duration and one settling curve.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when hovers, panel entrances and state changes all take the same short time and ease off at the end. Answer no when different controls move at visibly different speeds, or when a blurred layer is animated.

criterion: Every icon-only control on the signed-in screens carries a readable text name.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each control drawn as a glyph alone exposes a text name to a reader using the keyboard or a screen reader. Answer no when a glyph control is reachable with an empty name.

criterion: Every tappable control at phone width reaches the minimum touch target the responsive matrix pins.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every button, link and field a finger would use measures at least forty-four device pixels on both axes at phone width. Answer no when any of them is smaller on either axis.

criterion: The ambient rotation behind the event composer keeps turning for a visitor whose device asks for reduced motion.
evaluation_rule: This records a DEFECT, so yes means the failure was seen. Answer yes when the coloured ground behind the composer is still turning under a reduced-motion preference. Answer no when the ground holds its first frame and the named reveals arrive in their final state.

criterion: A dialog opened on the calendars screen hands focus back to the control that opened the dialog once the escape key closes the dialog.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when opening the dialog moves keyboard focus inside it, the escape key closes it, and focus lands back on the control that opened it. Answer no when focus stays behind the dialog, or when closing the dialog drops focus at the top of the document.

criterion: At phone width the guest list on the event management screen shows one card per guest carrying the column words as labels.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the guest table becomes a stack of cards at phone width and every value keeps its header word beside it. Answer no when the table keeps its columns and has to be scrolled sideways at that width.

criterion: A rejected sign in answers with a short shake of the card and a sentence beneath the field.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a wrong password moves the card a few pixels from side to side once and a sentence appears under the field. Answer no when the card holds still, or when the outcome is marked by colour alone.

criterion: A notice raised on the event management screen carries its status hue as a narrow leading edge rather than as a fill behind the words.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the coloured part of the notice is a thin bar on one side and the words sit on the ordinary panel ground. Answer no when the whole notice is washed in the status colour.

criterion: The discover list paints skeleton blocks shaped like the cards still arriving rather than a centred spinner.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the first paint shows grey blocks in the shape of the cards and the cards replace them in place. Answer no when a spinner sits in the middle of an empty page, or when the layout jumps once the data lands.

criterion: No dependency appears in either package manifest that no checklist obligation required, and none of them is a mail vendor SDK, a queue client, a cache client, an object-store client or a second database driver.
evaluation_rule: A dependency is a package named in a runtime dependency block of either package manifest -- the Angular frontend's or the Hono backend's -- not a transitive lock entry and not a development-only tool. Yes if every runtime dependency is Angular, Hono, the TypeScript runtime support those two need, the PostgreSQL driver, the SMTP mail client, or a direct requirement of one of those. No if either manifest names a mail vendor SDK such as SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark or Resend, a queue client such as BullMQ, Kafka or RabbitMQ, a cache client such as Redis or Memcached, an object-store client such as an S3 SDK, a second database driver such as MySQL, SQLite or MongoDB, or any package no checklist obligation reaches.

criterion: No table, column or seed row exists beyond the five tables the obligation list enumerates: accounts, calendars, events, registrations and email_log.
evaluation_rule: A table is a relation the schema or a migration creates, a column is a column on one of those relations, and a seed row is a row the seed routine writes. Yes if the schema creates exactly accounts, calendars, events, registrations and email_log, every column on them serves a field the brief's data model names, and the seed writes only the five pinned accounts, the two pinned calendars, the seeded events and their seeded registrations. No if the schema creates a sixth relation such as sessions, tokens, jobs, audit_log or notifications, adds a column no obligation reaches, or the seed writes rows beyond the fixtures the brief pins.

criterion: No background worker, scheduled job or queue module exists in the source tree for registration, approval, check-in or mail, all of which the obligation list keeps inside the handler that performs them.
evaluation_rule: A background worker is a process or module that performs work outside the request that caused it -- a scheduled job, a cron registration, a timer that drives work, a queue producer or consumer, or a separate worker entrypoint. Yes if registration, approval, check-in and mail are each performed synchronously inside the handler that serves the request, and no such module exists anywhere in the source tree. No if the tree contains a worker or jobs entrypoint, a cron or scheduling library registration, a setInterval or setTimeout that drives registration, approval, check-in or mail, or a queue module through which any of those four is deferred.

criterion: No image file, icon font or fetched web font ships in the source tree, and no surface the obligation list names as absent was built anyway: no insights screen, no moderation queue, no inbox, no invitation flow, no third-party sign-in.
evaluation_rule: An image file is a raster or vector asset shipped in the tree -- png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg or ico; an icon font or fetched web font is a font binary -- woff, woff2, ttf, otf or eot -- shipped in the tree, or pulled in from a font package or remote font stylesheet the application imports. The host's own approval queue on the guest management screen is required by the brief and is never a violation of this criterion. Yes if every symbol and every cover is drawn by code, the tree neither ships nor imports any such image or font asset, and none of the named absent surfaces was built. No if the tree ships an image or font file, imports a font package or a remote font stylesheet, or contains an insights or attendance charting screen, a site-wide administration or content-moderation queue separate from the host's approval queue, an inbox or messaging surface, an invitation flow, or a third-party sign-in control.

criterion: One naming convention runs across the source for the same idea, so a seat held is not a seat in one module and a place in another, and the stored enum spellings the obligation list pins are the spellings the code uses end to end.
evaluation_rule: One naming convention means one word for one idea everywhere it appears in the source. Yes if a single term names the seat a confirmed registration holds across the schema, the API and the view layer, and the stored enum spellings the brief pins -- draft, published, registration_closed and cancelled for an event, and pending_approval, confirmed, waitlisted, declined, checked_in, cancelled_by_guest and cancelled_by_host for a registration -- are the spellings the code writes, sends and matches end to end. No if two modules name the same idea differently, so a seat is a seat in one and a place, spot or slot in another, or if any layer stores, emits or compares a variant spelling such as checkedIn, cancelled_by_user or registration-closed.

criterion: The seat-holding rule is implemented in one transactional place and called from registration, cancellation, approval and the capacity raise, rather than being restated per route.
evaluation_rule: The seat-holding rule is the logic deciding whether a registration takes a seat, a waiting-list place or a refusal, and keeping registrations in confirmed or checked_in from exceeding capacity. Yes if that decision is written once, inside a single database transaction, in one named function or module, and registration, cancellation, host approval and the capacity raise all reach it through that one entry point. No if two or more of those four paths restate the capacity comparison, the waiting-list positioning or the seat release inline in their own route handler, so the same rule exists in more than one place and the paths could disagree on the last seat.

criterion: The theme derivation is written once in a server-side module and imported by the view layer as tokens, rather than reimplemented inside individual components.
evaluation_rule: Theme derivation is the computation turning an event's stored key colour into the ground, ink, heading and hairline values that event page paints. Yes if that computation lives in one server-side module and the view layer consumes its output as tokens -- CSS custom properties or an equivalent token object -- without recomputing it. No if a component derives a tint, a contrast decision or the too-pale readability fallback from the key colour itself, or if the same derivation appears both in a server module and in a client component, so the two could disagree on the same event's palette.

criterion: The pinned literals the obligation list names -- the seven mail subject lines, the CSV header line, the reserved paths, the twelve category names and the pinned copy strings -- are declared once and read from that declaration in every path that needs them, rather than duplicated as inline literals.
evaluation_rule: A pinned literal is a string the brief fixes exactly: the seven mail subject lines, the CSV header line email,display_name,status,waitlist_position,ticket_code, the eleven reserved paths, the twelve category names, and the pinned copy strings such as No Events Found, No Calendars Yet, No Guests Yet and Create Event. Yes if each such literal is declared once, in a constant or module, and every path needing it reads it from that declaration. No if a mail subject line, the CSV header, the reserved path list, the category list or a pinned copy string is written inline at a second use site, so two places would have to be edited to change one string.
